transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Forces in Yemen that are backed by Saudi Arabia say they've recaptured a port city from Houthi
rebels.
But this comes as Houthi rebels based in Yemen are firing into Saudi Arabia.
They claim they have hit Saudi oil sites over the past few days.
The Saudi government has not confirmed this.
NPR's Ea Betrawi says Saudi Arabia is now getting help.
To defend against these attacks, Saudi Arabia is getting some support from Britain and France.
Yesterday, top ministers from Pakistan and Turkey also met in Saudi Arabia, and they
confirmed that they're providing rapid military support now to the kingdom as part of the
Mecca agreement.
That's the new defense pact that was signed by the three countries over the summer.
And this pact really stems from President Trump's reluctance to get directly involved in another
war in the Gulf.
The U.S. has not agreed to Saudi Arabia's request for refueling support, but it is sharing
intel on the Houthis.
NPR's Ea Betrawi reporting.
The White House did not allow reporters from the media organization Politico to fly on Air
Force One yesterday.
That was for President Trump's trip to Nebraska.
Politico and President Trump are in active litigation over the news outlet's right to
cover him.
NPR's Julianna Kim reports.
A Politico spokesperson confirmed to NPR that the publication was excluded from Monday's
press pool, which refers to a group of reporters traveling with the president.
Politico, along with CNN and MSNow, was barred from the White House last month before they
filed a lawsuit, and a judge ordered the Trump administration to temporarily restore access.
The outlets accused Trump of retaliating because of what he says is unfavorable coverage of
him.
In a statement, the White House said traveling with the president on Air Force One is a privilege,
not a right.
The next hearing on the case is scheduled for Thursday.
Julianna Kim, NPR News.
President Trump will visit a port just outside Baltimore, Maryland, today.
He's scheduled to speak at an event hosted by defense contractors and dural industries.
The port is very close to where the Key Bridge collapsed in March 2024.
It had been hit by a container ship leaving Baltimore.
Six workers were killed.
The Nobel Prize in physics has gone to a researcher who led an effort to build a giant particle
detector in Antarctica.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield has more on what it found.
Francis Hallson has spent his career chasing ghostly particles known as neutrinos.
Neutrinos rarely interact with regular matter, but when they do, they create a tiny flash
of light.
Hallson, at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, developed a plan to place detectors in a cubic
kilometer of ice in Antarctica.
At the time, it seemed like a long shot.
The detector, called Ice Cube, won the prize for finding high-energy neutrinos from deep
space.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
An American citizen who was shot and wounded by Border Patrol agents in Chicago is now
suing the government.
Mariamar Martinez, a teacher's assistant, was shot five times.
She alleges that shooting was not justified and that the agents were never in danger.
Schools across the country have long struggled to hire and keep teachers in areas such as
special education, math, and science.
NPR's Janaki Mehta reports most states are not using higher pay to help fill those jobs.
Extra pay is known to help attract and retain teachers, but the National Council on Teacher
Quality found 32 states offer no additional pay to draw and keep teachers in hard-to-fill
schools or subjects.
And the study says states are actually moving away from those kinds of incentives.
Only 13 states pay teachers extra for working in schools that have high turnover (that number
is down from 28 states in 2022), and only 17 states pay teachers more to work in hard-to-staff
subjects like math, science, or special ed (that's down from 22 states in 2022).
The report shows that high schools are struggling most at keeping teachers, especially those
serving families with low incomes.
All this comes as states face tighter budgets across the country.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
Disgraced tell evangelist Jim Baker has died at the age of 86.
That's according to his wife, Lori Baker.
Jim Baker and his former wife, Tammy Faye Baker, built a Christian TV empire called the PTL
Club.
He passed that over as sex, scandal, and financial crimes, for which he spent time in prison.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Saudi-backed forces in Yemen recapture port city from Houthi rebels; Houthis fire into Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia receives military support from Britain, France, Pakistan, Turkey against Houthi attacks
White House excludes Politico reporters from Air Force One during President Trump's Nebraska trip
Politico sues Trump administration over press access; next hearing scheduled for Thursday
President Trump to visit port outside Baltimore, Maryland near collapsed Key Bridge site
Nobel Prize in physics awarded to researcher Francis Hallson for neutrino detector in Antarctica
American citizen Mariamar Martinez sues government after being shot by Border Patrol agents in Chicago
Most states not using higher pay to attract and retain teachers in hard-to-fill subjects
Disgraced televangelist Jim Baker dies at age 86; built PTL Club with former wife Tammy Faye
